newsitem.title: DENMARK: Red Cross vows to help beleaguered Albania. [corrected 19:57 gmt]
newsitem.headline: Red Cross vows to help beleaguered Albania. [corrected 19:57 gmt]

text.p: Representatives of 50 European Red Cross and Red Crescent groups meeting to assess future joint humanitarian activity in Europe vowed on Monday to support Albania.

"The conference plans to adopt a resolution in support of the Albanian Red Cross and its work in helping the victims of the revolt in Albania," the Red Cross and Red Crescent said in a statement issued at the opening of a four-day meeting.

It said that the Albanian Red Cross was unable to attend the conference but had sent a message describing extensive plundering and destruction of its stores, offices and supply depots in Albania during the present unrest.

"The violence (in Albania) has not only involved robbery, arson and the destruction of economic, financial, social and administrative institutions, it has also left many dead and hundreds of wounded," the message from Albania said.
"Red Cross emergency depots have been raided and some of our local offices have been destroyed," it added.

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) (corrects from International Red Cross Federation (ICRC)) has set up a mission in Tirana, the Albanian capital, and is preparing to open an office in the south of the country, they said.

"Surgical material and medical assistance for 400 wounded has been delivered for hospitals and a senior delegate is to join the IFRC team in Tirana when travel is possible," the conference statement said.

Earlier the Copenhagen conference, hosted by the Danish Red Cross and sister national societies in Norway, Sweden, Finland and Iceland, was formally opened by Danish prime minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen.
"Seventy-four million people are living on or below the poverty line in Europe," he told the 300 delegates.
"The Red Cross has a special role to play, helping before governments are able to intervene and staying on after they have left," he said.

The conference, running until March 20, brings together the Red Cross and the Moslem Red Crescent organisations at national and international level, governmental and non-governmental as well as voluntary organisations and United Nations observers.
It is the first meeting of Red Cross and Crescent societies from both sides of the old ideological divide in Europe since communism fell.
